name: Forehand block
summary: A short, firm stroke close to the table that sends a topspin ball back using its own speed.
whenToUse: Against a fast or heavy topspin to your forehand when you have no time to loop, or when you want to stay close and move the ball around.

keyPoints.stance: Close to the table, feet a little wider than shoulders, knees bent, right foot slightly back (left foot if left-handed).
keyPoints.bodyAction: Very little. A small turn of the waist to line the bat up, then hold your shape.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Tiny. The bat starts in front and moves a few centimetres forward; no backswing.
keyPoints.timing: Early: just after the bounce, on the rise.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Close, about half a metre from the end line.
keyPoints.freeArm: Up and in front for balance.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow in front of the body, bat slightly closed. The heavier the topspin, the more closed the bat.
keyPoints.recovery: Bat back to the middle straight away: the next ball comes fast.
keyPoints.anticipation: Watch the looper's swing: a longer, more upward swing means more spin, so close the bat more.

cues: Close the face over the ball

learningPath.task: Watch the 3D player block from the side. Notice there is almost no swing.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along: hold the bat in front, small forward push, back to ready.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Was there no backswing at all?
Did you come back to ready each time?

learningPath.task: Block slow topspin balls to one spot. Just find the angle.
Block a steady loop until 15 in a row.
Block from both wings, switching side.
Play loop-against-block points as the blocker.
Test: forehand blocks in a row.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent loops hard to your forehand and you are close to the table.
gamePatterns.how: Block to the wide backhand or into their playing elbow. Change the angle, not the speed.

gamePatterns.situation: A long rally where you are under pressure.
gamePatterns.how: Block once to buy time, then step back in and attack the next ball.

causes: Bat too open for the spin
fixes: Close the bat more against heavy topspin
Relax and let the ball rebound

troubleshooting.symptom: The ball goes into the net
causes: Bat too closed for a light topspin
Contact too late, as the ball drops
fixes: Open the bat a little against light spin
Move in and take it earlier

troubleshooting.symptom: I'm too slow, the ball beats me
fixes: Keep the bat in front at table height
Stay half a metre from the table

penholdNotes: Penholders block with the same face; turn the wrist so the face points forward-down.
